claims.statement: Any nonnegative row detector equal to one on every failed row excludes failures when its total mass is below one.
A preregistered row-dependent exponential detector equals one on a zero row; if its temperatures are at most the frozen uniform temperature, its success implies frozen INT-AOD.
The occupancy detector is the expected number of uncovered rows under independent candidate-offset sampling.
Sampling exactly K of M candidate offsets misses a row with Z successful offsets with probability binom(M-Z,K)/binom(M,K).
The exact constant-density cover has degree Theta(X^2/log X).
At preregistered temperature tau asymp log N/X, the exact cover degree falls to Theta(X), and a successful detector implies frozen INT-AOD.

An equal mixture of Poisson row classes separated by Theta(X) has a Laplace-transform zero at distance Theta(1/X), outside the useful tau asymp log X/X scale. Whole-block cumulant convergence does not follow from rowwise Poisson behaviour alone.
A polylogarithmic row partition with a convergent ordinary-cumulant bound exceeding log(n_b B) in every stratum implies INT-AOD.
Each ordinary cumulant of Z=sum_m I_m is the sum of common-row joint cumulants over all ordered prime-offset column tuples, including repetitions.
The safe dependency graph is complete and its temperature-weighted activity is Theta(log X), excluding generic constant-threshold absolute cluster criteria.
Stratified ordinary-cumulant growth with dependence scale D_b << X/(log X)^(1+delta) implies INT-SOCB and hence INT-AOD.
Row-uniform Hardy-Littlewood factorial-moment estimates through K=Theta(log X), with the explicit weighted one-row error budget, imply INT-AOD.
The exact divisor decomposition reaches a sparse one-offset-per-modulus hyperbola beyond sqrt(H); a new signed rowwise bilinear theorem would imply INT-AOD but no established theorem supplies it.
Finite primorial panels and adversarial incidence matrices select and falsify methods but do not prove asymptotic Fortune statements.
